   974	
   975	## 8. Resource Policy Integration
   976	
   977	Every tunable in the implementation MUST be resolved from
   978	`TurnlockResourcePolicy` (section 2.2). No hardcoded constants for limits,
   979	timeouts, grace periods, or capacities.
   980	
   981	The Turnlock adapter is responsible for constructing the policy from the
   982	committed `STD-TURNLOCK-DELEGATION-RESOURCE-POLICY` before calling
   983	`createTurnlockIntegration`.
   984	
   985	If the policy changes between runs (detected via `resourcePolicyDigest`),
   986	Turnlock creates a new `TurnlockIntegration` instance with the updated policy.
   987	The registry is policy-versioned via its `version` field.
   988	
   989	---
   990	
   991	## 9. Migration from Current API
   992	
   993	### 9.1 Backward compatibility
   994	
   995	The existing RPC event-bus interface (`registerSubagentRpcBridge`) and all
   996	interactive Pi functionality MUST continue to work unchanged. The Turnlock
   997	integration is a separate sub-path export.
   998	
   999	### 9.2 Sub-path contract
  1000	
  1001	```typescript
  1002	// Public, stable, side-effect-free on load.
  1003	import { createTurnlockIntegration } from "pi-subagents/turnlock";
  1004	```
  1005	
  1006	The sub-path MUST NOT:
  1007	
  1008	- Import or initialize the Pi extension (`ExtensionAPI`)
  1009	- Start the result watcher
  1010	- Register TUI components
  1011	- Touch `globalThis` singletons (background-work registry, etc.)
  1012	- Open files, create directories, or acquire locks at import time
  1013	
  1014	### 9.3 Result watcher coexistence
  1015	
  1016	Turnlock result files live under `<registryRoot>/launches/<id>/results/`,
  1017	completely outside `RESULTS_DIR`. No watcher modification needed.
  1018	
  1019	### 9.4 File structure
  1020	
  1021	```
  1022	<registryRoot>/                  ← Turnlock-allocated
  1023	├── lock
  1024	├── registry.json
  1025	└── launches/
  1026	    └── <dependencyExecutionId>/
  1027	        ├── async/               ← launcher working dir
  1028	        └── results/             ← job result files (write-once, retained until ack)
  1029	```
  1030	
  1031	---
  1032	
  1033	## 10. Non-Requirements (Explicit Exclusions)
  1034	
  1035	This specification does NOT require:
  1036	
  1037	- **Remote execution.** All launches run as local child processes.
  1038	- **Network resilience.** Assumes a local APFS filesystem.
  1039	- **Multi-machine coordination.** O_EXCL lock is local.
  1040	- **Exactly-once LLM execution.** Durability covers launch tracking and result
  1041	  retention, not LLM request deduplication.
  1042	- **Authentication / authorization.** Caller is a trusted local process.
  1043	- **Encryption at rest.**
  1044	- **Compression or archival.**
  1045	- **Graceful degradation under disk full.** Operations fail with filesystem
  1046	  errors. Atomic writes leave the registry consistent.
  1047	- **Registry backup or replication.**
  1048	- **Horizontal scaling.** One Turnlock instance, one registry.
  1049	
  1050	---
  1051	
  1052	## 11. Acceptance Checklist
  1053	
  1054	Before Turnlock's Dependency Contract can declare this implementation
  1055	compatible, ALL of the following MUST be true:
  1056	
  1057	- [ ] `capabilities()` returns all 7 capability booleans as `true`
  1058	- [ ] `sourceCommit` embedded at build time, matches inspected commit
  1059	- [ ] `registryRoot` is mandatory; no default, no env fallback
  1060	- [ ] Sub-path `pi-subagents/turnlock` has zero side effects on load
  1061	- [ ] `launchStaticGroup` is idempotent for equal key+digest
  1062	- [ ] `launchStaticGroup` returns `"conflict"` for divergent digest
  1063	- [ ] `launchStaticGroup` progresses orphaned `dispatch-intent` (ensure-launch)
  1064	- [ ] Registry entry is durable before `"accepted"` reply
  1065	- [ ] `inspectLaunch` returns correct state after process restart
  1066	- [ ] Stale-run reconciliation updates the durable registry
  1067	- [ ] Result files survive process crash and restart
  1068	- [ ] `readJobResult` never deletes or modifies result files
  1069	- [ ] Result immutability: modification → `IntegrityConflictError`, not silent update
  1070	- [ ] `ArtifactTargetRefV1` path confinement enforced (no `..`, no symlink escape)
  1071	- [ ] `stopLaunch` is idempotent and works after restart
  1072	- [ ] `acknowledgeRetention` deletes results only when explicitly called
  1073	- [ ] `acknowledgeRetention` is idempotent on retry
  1074	- [ ] All limits/timeouts/capacities resolved from `TurnlockResourcePolicy`, not hardcoded
  1075	- [ ] Lock: bootId + PID + nonce; stale detection uses both; inode check on release
  1076	- [ ] Corrupted lock file → `registry-locked`, not silent removal
  1077	- [ ] All test categories from section 7 pass against actual implementation
  1078	- [ ] Scale benchmark at policy max entries published
  1079	- [ ] Existing Pi subagent functionality unchanged
  1080	- [ ] No runtime dependency added beyond those already present in the fork
  1081	
  1082	---
  1083	
  1084	## A. Design Decisions
  1085	
  1086	### A.1 Why same-process, not Unix socket?
  1087	
  1088	The Turnlock Runner and Pi strategy adapter run in the same Bun process. A
  1089	direct TypeScript API is simpler, avoids serialization, and keeps the
  1090	dependency graph explicit. The socket becomes relevant only if/when Turnlock
  1091	and Pi run in separate processes.
  1092	
  1093	### A.2 Why ensure-launch semantics in launchStaticGroup?
  1094	
  1095	A separate `reconcileLaunch` operation was considered. Having
  1096	`launchStaticGroup` automatically progress an orphaned `dispatch-intent` is
  1097	simpler for the caller: the same idempotent call that creates a launch also
  1098	recovers a crashed one. The caller does not need to branch on `inspectLaunch`
  1099	output before retrying.
  1100	
  1101	### A.3 Why ArtifactTargetRefV1 instead of raw paths?
  1102	
  1103	Raw absolute paths allow the caller to write anywhere. `ArtifactTargetRefV1`
  1104	confines writes to a trusted root, enforces write-once semantics, and enables
  1105	integrity verification via `ArtifactCommitmentV2`. This matches Turnlock's
  1106	artifact system.
  1107	
  1108	### A.4 Why write-once + integrity conflict, not mutable results?
  1109	
  1110	Turnlock's `snapshot-authoritative` principle: facts, once established, cannot
  1111	be silently revised. If a result file changes after the initial write, this is
  1112	evidence of an integrity violation (disk corruption, external tampering, or
  1113	implementation bug), not a normal state update. Quarantine preserves the
  1114	evidence for operator disposition.
  1115	
  1116	### A.5 Why bootId in the lock file?
  1117	
  1118	macOS reuses PIDs. A stale lock check based on PID alone can falsely conclude
  1119	a dead holder is alive if the PID was recycled. `bootId + PID` eliminates this:
  1120	a recycled PID after a reboot has a different bootId. Within the same boot,
  1121	PID reuse is possible but extremely unlikely within the lock timeout; the
  1122	nonce provides an additional layer of defense.
  1123	
  1124	### A.6 Why fsync on temp file AND parent directory?
  1125	
  1126	`rename` is atomic on APFS, but without `fsync` on the parent directory, the
  1127	directory entry may not be persisted before a crash. The combination
  1128	`fsync(temp) → rename → fsync(parentDir)` guarantees that after a crash, either
  1129	the old file or the new file is visible, and the new file's contents are
  1130	complete.
  1131

    44	  never via private `src/` imports.
    45	- **Zero side effects on load.** No TUI, no watcher, no `ExtensionAPI`
    46	  requirement, no singleton module-level state, no I/O at import time.
    47	- **Not a Turnlock core dependency.** The `pi-subagents` package is pinned by
    48	  the strategy adapter's Dependency Contract, not by the Turnlock runtime core.
    49	
    50	### 0.2 What this changes relative to the current RPC API (v0.35.1)
    51	
    52	| Concern | Current (v0.35.1) | Required (v2) |
    53	| ------- | ----------------- | ------------- |
    54	| Launch identity | Generated by pi-subagents | Caller-chosen durable key, committed before spawn |
    55	| Idempotency | None | Equal key+digest → same launch; divergent → conflict |
    56	| Acknowledgment | Best-effort RPC reply on event bus | Durable registry write before reply |
    57	| Post-restart lookup | Directory scan + in-memory state | `inspectLaunch(callerLaunchKey)` reads durable registry |
    58	| Result lifecycle | Deleted by watcher after first read | Retained until explicit `acknowledgeRetention` |
    59	| Result immutability | N/A | Write-once; modification → integrity conflict, not silent update |
    60	| Stop | Session-scoped, running-only | Idempotent by caller key, works post-restart |
    61	| Session coupling | All operations require active Pi session | Launch uses internal Pi executor; other ops are sessionless |
    62	| Launch progress | Fire-and-forget async | Durable FSM with ensure-launch recovery of stalled intents |
    63	
    64	### 0.3 Environment
    65	
    66	Same as the current fork: Node.js ≥22, macOS APFS, local filesystem, single
    67	machine. Durability relies on atomic file rename on a local copy-on-write
    68	filesystem. No networked filesystem, no Docker overlay, no NFS.
    69

    71	
    72	## 1. Durable Registry
    73	
    74	### 1.1 Storage location
    75	
    76	`registryRoot` is a **mandatory** constructor parameter. No default, no
    77	fallback to `~/.pi/...`, no environment variable. Turnlock allocates and
    78	provides the root. This ensures the registry lives inside Turnlock's managed
    79	workspace and is subject to its lifecycle (cleanup, retention, access control).
    80	
    81	```typescript
    82	interface TurnlockIntegrationOptions {
    83	  /** Absolute path to the registry root directory. REQUIRED. */
    84	  readonly registryRoot: string;
    85	  // ...
    86	}
    87	```
    88	
    89	### 1.2 Registry entries
    90	
    91	One entry per launch, keyed by `callerLaunchKey`:
    92	
    93	```typescript
    94	interface RegistryFile {
    95	  readonly version: 2;
    96	  readonly entries: Record<string, RegistryEntry>;
    97	}
    98	
    99	interface RegistryEntry {
   100	  readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   101	  readonly requestDigest: string;             // hex SHA-256
   102	  readonly groupSpecDigest: string;           // hex SHA-256
   103	  readonly dependencyExecutionId: string;     // ULID
   104	  readonly state: DurableLaunchState;
   105	  readonly asyncDir: string;                  // absolute, under registryRoot
   106	  readonly resultNamespace: string;           // absolute root for job results
   107	  readonly jobs: Record<string, RegistryJobEntry>;
   108	  readonly launchPlan: LaunchPlan;            // immutable, complete
   109	  readonly createdAtEpochMs: number;
   110	  readonly updatedAtEpochMs: number;
   111	  // Present only when state is terminal:
   112	  readonly terminalAtEpochMs?: number;
   113	  // Present only if stopLaunch was called:
   114	  readonly stopRequestedAtEpochMs?: number;
   115	  readonly stopReason?: string;
   116	}
   117	
   118	/**
   119	 * Durable launch FSM.
   120	 *
   121	 *   dispatch-intent   ← registry written, no child process yet
   122	 *        │
   123	 *   launcher-started  ← child process spawned, PID recorded
   124	 *        │
   125	 *   running           ← handshake complete, agents executing
   126	 *        │
   127	 *   completed | failed | stopped   ← terminal
   128	 */
   129	type DurableLaunchState =
   130	  | "dispatch-intent"
   131	  | "launcher-started"
   132	  | "running"
   133	  | "completed"
   134	  | "failed"
   135	  | "stopped";
   136	
   137	/**
   138	 * Immutable launch plan. Stored in the registry at dispatch-intent time so
   139	 * that a recovery process can mechanically determine whether the launch was
   140	 * started, and if not, safely trigger it.
   141	 */
   142	interface LaunchPlan {
   143	  readonly version: 1;
   144	  readonly concurrency: number;
   145	  readonly deadlineAtEpochMs: number;
   146	  readonly jobs: readonly LaunchPlanJob[];
   147	}
   148	
   149	interface LaunchPlanJob {
   150	  readonly jobId: string;
   151	  readonly agentName: string;
   152	  readonly task: string;
   153	  readonly modelSelector: string;
   154	  readonly requestedThinking?: string;
   155	  readonly targetRef: ArtifactTargetRefV1;
   156	  readonly resultContractDigest?: string;
   157	}
   158	
   159	interface RegistryJobEntry {
   160	  readonly jobId: string;
   161	  readonly state: JobState;
   162	  readonly targetRef: ArtifactTargetRefV1;
   163	  /** Commitment published when the job reaches a terminal state. */
   164	  readonly resultCommitment?: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   165	  readonly terminalAtEpochMs?: number;
   166	}
   167	
   168	type JobState =
   169	  | "queued"
   170	  | "running"
   171	  | "completed"
   172	  | "failed"
   173	  | "stopped";
   174	```
   175	
   176	### 1.3 Atomic writes
   177	
   178	Every write to `registry.json` MUST use the pattern:
   179	
   180	```
   181	write temp file → fsync temp file → rename over target → fsync parent directory
   182	```
   183	
   184	The existing `writeAtomicJson` helper in `src/shared/atomic-json.ts` MUST be
   185	augmented with `fsync` on the file before rename and `fsync` on the parent
   186	directory after rename. On APFS, `rename` is atomic by design; the directory
   187	`fsync` guarantees the directory entry is persisted.
   188	
   189	### 1.4 Concurrency
   190	
   191	Single-writer via O_EXCL lock at `<registryRoot>/lock`. Readers do not need
   192	the lock (atomic rename guarantees consistent reads).
   193	
   194	The lock file MUST contain: `bootId`, `pid`, and a random `nonce`. Stale lock
   195	detection checks: `bootId` match AND `pid` alive. PID alone is insufficient
   196	(macOS reuses PIDs).
   197	
   198	The lock holder MUST NOT release a lock it did not acquire. Before `unlink`,
   199	verify the lock file's inode matches the one opened at acquisition. A corrupted
   200	or unreadable lock file MUST be treated as an indeterminate state, not silently
   201	removed.
   202	
   203	Lock timeout, lock acquisition retry interval, and stale lock grace period
   204	MUST be derived from the resource policy (section 8), not hardcoded.
   205	
   206	### 1.5 Registry scale
   207	
   208	The maximum number of concurrent entries and the maximum registry file size
   209	MUST be derived from the resource policy. The implementation MUST benchmark
   210	read/write performance at the policy-defined maximum and publish the results
   211	as part of the Dependency Contract evidence.
   212	
   213	Rewriting the entire registry file on every update is acceptable for the
   214	policy-defined scale. If the policy maximum exceeds what a single JSON file
   215	can handle, the storage design MUST be revisited (e.g., per-launch entry
   216	files with a manifest index).

   361	### 2.5 launchStaticGroup(request)
   362	
   363	```typescript
   364	interface LaunchJobRequest {
   365	  readonly jobId: string;
   366	  readonly agentName: string;
   367	  readonly task: string;
   368	  readonly modelSelector: string;
   369	  readonly requestedThinking?: string;
   370	  /** Turnlock-allocated, write-once, relative to a trusted root. */
   371	  readonly rawResultTarget: ArtifactTargetRefV1;
   372	  readonly resultContractDigest?: string;
   373	}
   374	
   375	interface LaunchRequest {
   376	  readonly apiVersion: "turnlock-pi-subagents-v1";
   377	  readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   378	  readonly requestDigest: string;
   379	  readonly groupSpecDigest: string;
   380	  readonly context: "fresh";
   381	  readonly failFast: false;
   382	  readonly concurrency: number;
   383	  readonly deadlineAtEpochMs: number;
   384	  readonly jobs: readonly LaunchJobRequest[];
   385	}
   386	
   387	type LaunchReply =
   388	  | {
   389	      readonly kind: "accepted";
   390	      readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   391	      readonly requestDigest: string;
   392	      readonly dependencyExecutionId: string;
   393	      /** Commitment to the durable registry record. */
   394	      readonly durableRecordCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   395	    }
   396	  | {
   397	      readonly kind: "already-accepted";
   398	      readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   399	      readonly requestDigest: string;
   400	      readonly dependencyExecutionId: string;
   401	      readonly durableRecordCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   402	    }
   403	  | {
   404	      readonly kind: "conflict";
   405	      readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   406	      readonly existingRequestDigest: string;
   407	    };
   408	```
   409	
   410	**Pre-conditions (validated synchronously, before any I/O):**
   411	
   412	- `callerLaunchKey` matches `/^[\w\-.\/:]{1,256}$/`, contains no `\0`
   413	- `requestDigest` and `groupSpecDigest` are exactly 64 lowercase hex chars
   414	- `jobs.length` ∈ [1, `resourcePolicy.maxJobsPerLaunch`]
   415	- All `jobId` values are unique within the request
   416	- All `rawResultTarget` resolve to distinct, confined paths under the launch
   417	  namespace root (see section 4)
   418	- `concurrency` ∈ [1, 4]
   419	- `deadlineAtEpochMs` > `Date.now()`
   420	
   421	**Algorithm:**
   422	
   423	1. Validate pre-conditions. Reject with `"invalid-request"` on failure.
   424	2. Acquire registry lock.
   425	3. Read `registry.json`.
   426	4. If an entry exists for `callerLaunchKey`:
   427	   a. If `entry.requestDigest === request.requestDigest`:
   428	      - If `entry.state === "dispatch-intent"`: this is a crashed-before-spawn
   429	        scenario. Progress: spawn launcher, transition to `"launcher-started"`,
   430	        write registry, release lock, return `"already-accepted"`.
   431	      - Otherwise: release lock, return `"already-accepted"`.
   432	   b. If `entry.requestDigest !== request.requestDigest`:
   433	      - Release lock, return `"conflict"`.
   434	5. Generate `dependencyExecutionId` (ULID).
   435	6. Build the immutable `LaunchPlan` from the request.
   436	7. Create `asyncDir` and `resultNamespace` under
   437	   `<registryRoot>/launches/<dependencyExecutionId>/`.
   438	8. Write registry entry with `state: "dispatch-intent"`, `launchPlan`, all jobs
   439	   in `"queued"` state:
   440	   - Atomic write (tmp + rename + fsync dir).
   441	9. Compute `durableRecordCommitment` = `ArtifactCommitmentV2` over the
   442	   written entry (digest of canonical JSON of the entry at rest).
   443	10. Spawn the launcher child process:
   444	    - Transition to `"launcher-started"`, record PID, write registry.
   445	11. Release lock.
   446	12. Return `{ kind: "accepted", ..., durableRecordCommitment }`.
   447	
   448	**Ensure-launch semantics:** `launchStaticGroup` is not just "create if
   449	absent." When called with a key in `"dispatch-intent"` state (written before
   450	a crash that killed the launcher), it MUST progress to `"launcher-started"`
   451	and spawn the child process. The launch plan is already in the registry; the
   452	implementation replays it deterministically.
   453	
   454	**Idempotency:** Same key+digest any number of times → exactly one execution
   455	group. Same key, different digest → `"conflict"` every time, no execution.
   456	
   457	### 2.6 inspectLaunch(callerLaunchKey)
   458	
   459	```typescript
   460	interface LaunchJobSnapshot {
   461	  readonly jobId: string;
   462	  readonly state: JobState;
   463	  readonly resultCommitment?: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   464	}
   465	
   466	interface LaunchSnapshot {
   467	  readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   468	  readonly requestDigest: string;
   469	  readonly dependencyExecutionId: string;
   470	  readonly state: DurableLaunchState;
   471	  readonly jobs: readonly LaunchJobSnapshot[];
   472	  readonly createdAtEpochMs: number;
   473	  readonly updatedAtEpochMs: number;
   474	  readonly terminalAtEpochMs?: number;
   475	  /** Commitment to the registry entry at the time of this snapshot. */
   476	  readonly snapshotCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   477	}
   478	```
   479	
   480	**Algorithm:**
   481	
   482	1. Read `registry.json` (no lock).
   483	2. If no entry for `callerLaunchKey`, throw `LaunchNotFoundError`.
   484	3. If `state` is `"launcher-started"` or `"running"`:
   485	   a. Read `asyncDir/status.json`.
   486	   b. If `status.json` has a `pid`, test liveness.
   487	   c. If the PID is dead AND `Date.now() - lastStatusUpdate > resourcePolicy.staleRunGraceMs`,
   488	      run stale-run reconciliation:
   489	      - Check each job's result target for a result file.
   490	      - Update job states and overall launch state based on evidence.
   491	      - Write updated registry (with lock).
   492	      - Return reconciled snapshot.
   493	4. Compute `snapshotCommitment` = canonical JSON digest of the entry as read.
   494	5. Return the snapshot.
   495	
   496	**No session requirement.** Reads only the durable registry.

   498	### 2.7 readJobResult(callerLaunchKey, jobId)
   499	
   500	```typescript
   501	type JobResult =
   502	  | { readonly kind: "not-terminal" }
   503	  | {
   504	      readonly kind: "available";
   505	      readonly jobId: string;
   506	      readonly terminalState: "completed" | "failed" | "stopped";
   507	      readonly resultCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   508	    };
   509	```
   510	
   511	**Algorithm:**
   512	
   513	1. Read `registry.json`.
   514	2. If no entry for `callerLaunchKey`, throw `LaunchNotFoundError`.
   515	3. If no job with `jobId`, throw `JobNotFoundError`.
   516	4. If job state is `"queued"` or `"running"`:
   517	   a. Check if a result file exists at the resolved `targetRef` path.
   518	   b. If yes and valid (UTF-8 JSON, ≤ `resourcePolicy.rawOutputBytesPerJob`):
   519	      - Compute `ArtifactCommitmentV2` (canonical JSON digest + byte size).
   520	      - Update registry: job state → `"completed"` (or `"failed"` based on
   521	        content), `resultCommitment`, `terminalAtEpochMs`.
   522	      - Return `{ kind: "available", terminalState, resultCommitment }`.
   523	   c. If no file, return `{ kind: "not-terminal" }`.
   524	5. If job state is terminal:
   525	   a. Verify result file exists at the resolved path.
   526	   b. Compute its `ArtifactCommitmentV2`.
   527	   c. If the commitment matches `registryEntry.jobs[jobId].resultCommitment`:
   528	      return `{ kind: "available", ... }`.
   529	   d. **If the commitment differs:** do NOT update the registry. Return an
   530	      `IntegrityConflictError` with both the recorded commitment and the
   531	      observed commitment. Turnlock treats this as a quarantine trigger.
   532	
   533	**Non-destructive guarantee:** This method MUST NOT delete, truncate, or modify
   534	the result file. The file remains until `acknowledgeRetention`.
   535	
   536	**Immutability guarantee:** A result file, once written, MUST NOT be modified
   537	by pi-subagents. If external modification is detected (commitment mismatch),
   538	this is an integrity conflict, not a normal result update.

   540	### 2.8 stopLaunch(callerLaunchKey, reason)
   541	
   542	```typescript
   543	interface StopReply {
   544	  readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   545	  readonly state: "stopping" | "stopped" | "already-terminal";
   546	  readonly jobs: readonly LaunchJobSnapshot[];
   547	  /** Commitment to the registry entry after the stop operation. */
   548	  readonly snapshotCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   549	}
   550	```
   551	
   552	**Algorithm:**
   553	
   554	1. Acquire registry lock.
   555	2. Read `registry.json`.
   556	3. If no entry, throw `LaunchNotFoundError`.
   557	4. If `entry.state` is terminal: release lock, return `"already-terminal"`.
   558	5. If `entry.state` is `"dispatch-intent"`: no process to kill. Transition
   559	   directly to `"stopped"`, mark all queued jobs as `"stopped"`. Write
   560	   registry. Release lock. Return `"stopped"`.
   561	6. If `entry.state` is `"launcher-started"` or `"running"`:
   562	   a. Record `stopRequestedAtEpochMs`, `stopReason`. Write registry (so the
   563	      stop intent is durable even if we crash next).
   564	   b. Release lock.
   565	   c. Send SIGTERM to the launcher PID.
   566	   d. Wait up to `resourcePolicy.stopGraceMs`.
   567	   e. If still alive: SIGKILL. Wait up to `resourcePolicy.stopGraceMs` again.
   568	   f. Re-acquire lock.
   569	   g. Transition state to `"stopped"`, set `terminalAtEpochMs`.
   570	   h. For each non-terminal job, set state `"stopped"`, `terminalAtEpochMs`.
   571	   i. Write atomic registry.
   572	   j. Release lock.
   573	   k. Return `"stopped"` with `snapshotCommitment`.
   574	
   575	**Idempotency:** Calling `stopLaunch` multiple times returns the same terminal
   576	state. No error on replay.

   578	### 2.9 acknowledgeRetention(callerLaunchKey, resultDigests)
   579	
   580	```typescript
   581	interface RetentionReply {
   582	  readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   583	  readonly acknowledgedDigests: Record<string, string>;
   584	  readonly earliestCleanupAtEpochMs: number;
   585	  /** Commitment to the retention receipt. */
   586	  readonly receiptCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   587	}
   588	```
   589	
   590	**Pre-conditions:**
   591	
   592	- Every `jobId` exists in the launch and is terminal.
   593	- Every digest matches the `resultCommitment.digest` in the registry AND the
   594	  current file on disk.
   595	
   596	**Algorithm:**
   597	
   598	1. Read `registry.json`.
   599	2. If no entry, throw `LaunchNotFoundError`.
   600	3. Validate all pre-conditions. On any failure, throw `RetentionConflictError`
   601	   with a `details` array listing each failed job and the specific mismatch.
   602	4. Acquire lock. Re-read and re-validate under lock.
   603	5. For each acknowledged job:
   604	   a. Delete the result file at the resolved path.
   605	   b. Delete intermediate artifacts under `asyncDir` for this job.
   606	   c. Mark job as `retentionAcknowledged: true` in registry.
   607	6. If all jobs acknowledged: mark launch for deferred cleanup.
   608	7. `earliestCleanupAtEpochMs = Date.now() + resourcePolicy.retentionFloorMs`.
   609	8. Compute `receiptCommitment` = artifact commitment over the acknowledgment
   610	   record.
   611	9. Write atomic registry. Release lock.
   612	10. Return `{ ..., earliestCleanupAtEpochMs, receiptCommitment }`.
   613	
   614	**Idempotency:** If called again with digests already acknowledged (files
   615	deleted), detect this from the registry and return success rather than
   616	throwing `RetentionConflictError`.

   628	  | "job-not-found"
   629	  | "integrity-conflict"       // result file modified since last read
   630	  | "retention-conflict"       // pre-conditions for acknowledgeRetention failed
   631	  | "registry-locked"
   632	  | "registry-corrupted"
   633	  | "too-many-entries"
   634	  | "invalid-caller-key"
   635	  | "invalid-request"
   636	  | "execution-failed";
   637	```
   638	
   639	---
   640	
   641	## 3. Launch Lifecycle
   642	
   643	### 3.1 Durable state machine
   644	
   645	```
   646	  launchStaticGroup(key, digest)
   647	         │
   648	         ▼
   649	   ┌──────────────┐
   650	   │dispatch-intent│  ← registry written, LaunchPlan stored, no child yet
   651	   └──────┬───────┘
   652	          │  spawn launcher child process
   653	          ▼
   654	   ┌────────────────┐
   655	   │launcher-started│  ← child PID recorded, handshake in progress
   656	   └──────┬─────────┘
   657	          │  handshake complete
   658	          ▼
   659	   ┌──────────┐
   660	   │ running  │──→ stopLaunch() or deadline ──→ ┌──────────┐
   661	   └────┬─────┘                                │ stopped  │
   662	        │                                      └──────────┘
   663	        │ (all jobs terminal)
   664	        ▼
   665	   ┌───────────┐     ┌──────────┐
   666	   │ completed │     │  failed  │
   667	   └─────┬─────┘     └────┬─────┘
   668	         │                │
   669	         └───────┬────────┘
   670	                 │  all results acknowledged
   671	                 ▼
   672	            ┌─────────┐
   673	            │ cleaned │  ← entry removed after retentionFloorMs
   674	            └─────────┘
   675	```
   676	
   677	### 3.2 Crash recovery at each state
   678	
   679	| State when crash occurs | Recovery via `launchStaticGroup` (same key+digest) | Recovery via `inspectLaunch` |
   680	| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
   681	| (no entry) | Creates new `dispatch-intent`, spawns launcher → `"accepted"` | `LaunchNotFoundError` |
   682	| `dispatch-intent` | Detects existing intent, **spawns launcher**, progresses to `"launcher-started"` → `"already-accepted"` | Returns `"dispatch-intent"`; caller can retry `launchStaticGroup` to progress |
   683	| `launcher-started` | Returns `"already-accepted"` | Checks PID liveness; if dead, stale-run reconciliation → `"failed"` |
   684	| `running` | Returns `"already-accepted"` | Checks PID liveness + status; may transition to terminal |
   685	| Any terminal | Returns `"already-accepted"` | Returns terminal snapshot |
   686	
   687	### 3.3 Reconciliation operation
   688	
   689	`inspectLaunch` is not purely observational. When it detects a dead launcher
   690	for a non-terminal launch:
   691	
   692	1. It MUST run stale-run reconciliation: check each job's result target,
   693	   determine terminal state, update the registry.
   694	2. It MUST NOT silently transition `"dispatch-intent"` to a terminal state
   695	   (there is no child to reconcile — the caller must re-invoke
   696	   `launchStaticGroup` to progress it).
   697	3. If evidence is ambiguous (some result files present, some missing, no
   698	   clear cause), it MUST NOT guess. Return the current state and let the
   699	   caller decide. Ambiguity is not failure.
   700	
   701	---
   702	
   703	## 4. Result Files
   704	
   705	### 4.1 ArtifactTargetRefV1 (not raw path strings)
   706	
   707	Turnlock allocates result targets using its artifact reference system:
   708	
   709	```typescript
   710	interface ArtifactTargetRefV1 {
   711	  readonly version: 1;
   712	  readonly root: "turnlock-run";
   713	  readonly allocationId: string;
   714	  readonly purpose: "strategy-raw-result";
   715	  readonly relativePath: string;
   716	}
   717	```
   718	
   719	The implementation MUST:
   720	
   721	1. Resolve `root` against the registry root (Turnlock provides the mapping).
   722	2. Validate that `relativePath` does not escape the root (no `..`, no
   723	   symlinks, no absolute components).
   724	3. Ensure the `allocationId` matches the launch namespace.
   725	4. Write exactly once — the file MUST NOT exist before writing.
   726	5. Publish an `ArtifactCommitmentV2` (canonical JSON digest + byte size) after
   727	   the write.
   728	
   729	### 4.2 Location
   730	
   731	Result files are written under
   732	`<registryRoot>/launches/<dependencyExecutionId>/results/`, resolved from the
   733	`ArtifactTargetRefV1`. This is OUTSIDE the standard `RESULTS_DIR` that the
   734	existing `result-watcher.ts` monitors. No watcher modification is needed.
   735	
   736	### 4.3 Format
   737	
   738	Valid UTF-8 JSON. Maximum `resourcePolicy.rawOutputBytesPerJob` bytes.
   739	
   740	If the runner output exceeds this limit: stop reading at the limit, mark the
   741	job `"failed"` with a structured error. Do NOT write truncated JSON (truncated
   742	JSON is often invalid and misleading). The error message MUST include the limit
   743	that was exceeded.
   744	
   745	Binary (non-UTF-8) content: mark job `"failed"`. Do not write an invalid
   746	result file.
   747	
   748	### 4.4 Immutability
   749	
   750	A result file is **write-once**. After the initial write, pi-subagents MUST NOT
   751	modify it. If `readJobResult` detects a change (digest mismatch from the
   752	recorded `resultCommitment`):
   753	
   754	- **Do NOT** update the registry's `resultCommitment`.
   755	- **Do NOT** treat it as a normal update.
   756	- Throw `IntegrityConflictError` with both the recorded and observed
   757	  commitments.
   758	- Turnlock treats this as a quarantine trigger.
   759	
   760	---
   761	
   762	## 5. Concurrency and Locking
   763	
   764	### 5.1 Lock file format
   765	
   766	```typescript
   767	interface LockFile {
   768	  readonly bootId: string;
   769	  readonly pid: number;
   770	  readonly nonce: string;       // random, 16 hex chars
   771	  readonly acquiredAtEpochMs: number;
   772	}
   773	```
   774	
   775	### 5.2 Lock acquisition
   776	
   777	```typescript
   778	function acquireLock(
   779	  registryRoot: string,
   780	  policy: TurnlockResourcePolicy
   781	): LockHandle {
   782	  const lockPath = path.join(registryRoot, "lock");
   783	  const deadline = Date.now() + policy.lockTimeoutMs;
   784	
   785	  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
   786	    try {
   787	      const fd = fs.openSync(lockPath, "wx");  // O_EXCL
   788	      const lockFile: LockFile = {
   789	        bootId: getBootId(),
   790	        pid: process.pid,
   791	        nonce: randomHex(16),
   792	        acquiredAtEpochMs: Date.now(),
   793	      };
   794	      fs.writeSync(fd, JSON.stringify(lockFile));
   795	      fs.fsyncSync(fd);
   796	      return {
   797	        fd,
   798	        path: lockPath,
   799	        inode: fs.fstatSync(fd).ino,
   800	        nonce: lockFile.nonce,
   801	      };
   802	    } catch (err) {
   803	      if (err.code !== "EEXIST") throw err;
   804	      const existing = readLockFile(lockPath);
   805	      if (existing === null) {
   806	        // Corrupted lock file — indeterminate state. Do NOT remove blindly.
   807	        sleepSync(policy.lockRetryIntervalMs);
   808	        continue;
   809	      }
   810	      if (!isLockHolderValid(existing, policy.staleLockGraceMs)) {
   811	        // Stale lock: bootId mismatch or PID dead past grace period.
   812	        try { fs.unlinkSync(lockPath); } catch {}
   813	        continue;
   814	      }
   815	      // Valid lock held by another process. Wait.
   816	      sleepSync(policy.lockRetryIntervalMs);
   817	    }
   818	  }
   819	  throw new TurnlockIntegrationError("registry-locked",
   820	    `Could not acquire registry lock within ${policy.lockTimeoutMs}ms.`);
   821	}
   822	```
   823	
   824	### 5.3 Lock release
   825	
   826	```typescript
   827	function releaseLock(handle: LockHandle): void {
   828	  // Verify we still own this lock file (inode match).
   829	  let currentIno: number | undefined;
   830	  try { currentIno = fs.statSync(handle.path).ino; } catch { return; }
   831	  if (currentIno !== handle.inode) return; // Replaced by another process.
   832	
   833	  try { fs.closeSync(handle.fd); } catch {}
   834	  try { fs.unlinkSync(handle.path); } catch {}
   835	}
   836	```
   837	
   838	### 5.4 Lock lifecycle
   839	
   840	- `process.on("exit", () => releaseLock(activeLock))` for normal exit.
   841	- Every lock acquisition is wrapped in try/finally with release in the finally
   842	  block.
   843	- If the process crashes, stale lock detection (bootId + PID liveness) allows
   844	  the next process to break it.
   845	
   846	---
   847	
   848	## 6. Internal Execution
   849	
   850	### 6.1 pi-subagents owns execution
   851	
   852	No `executeGroup` or `resolveAgent` callbacks in the public options.
   853	`createTurnlockIntegration` MUST internally:
   854	
   855	1. Resolve agent configurations using the existing agent discovery mechanism
   856	   (`discoverAgents` from `src/agents/agents.ts`).
   857	2. Build runner steps from the `LaunchPlan` jobs (reusing
   858	   `buildAsyncRunnerSteps` from `src/runs/background/async-execution.ts`).
   859	3. Spawn launcher child processes (reusing `spawnRunner`).
   860	4. Write job results to the `ArtifactTargetRefV1`-resolved paths.
   861	5. Update the durable registry on job completion.
   862	
   863	Agent configuration (profiles, models, tools, permissions) MUST be committed
   864	before `launchStaticGroup` is called. The agent resolution is part of the
   865	strategy preflight in the Turnlock adapter, not the integration API.
   866	
   867	### 6.2 Launcher handshake
   868	
   869	The existing `spawnRunner` startup handshake (ready → ack → acknowledged →
   870	proceed) MUST be preserved. The Turnlock integration adds:
   871	
   872	- After `proceed` is sent: transition registry from `"launcher-started"` to
   873	  `"running"`.
   874	- If the handshake fails (launcher dies before `proceed`): transition to
   875	  `"failed"` via standard stale-run reconciliation.
   876	
   877	### 6.3 Test doubles
   878	
   879	Test-only injection of the executor is acceptable ONLY through module-level
   880	test helpers, never through the public `TurnlockIntegrationOptions`:
   881	
   882	```typescript
   883	// For tests only — not exported from the public sub-path
   884	export function __test_createTurnlockIntegration(
   885	  options: TurnlockIntegrationOptions,
   886	  executorOverride: TestExecutor,
   887	): TurnlockIntegration;
   888	```
   889	
   890	---
   891	
   892	## 7. Test Requirements
   893	
   894	### 7.1 Registry durability
   895	
   896	| Test | Proves |
   897	| ---- | ------ |
   898	| Write `dispatch-intent`, SIGKILL process, new process reads entry | Registry survives crash |
   899	| 10 concurrent `inspectLaunch` during atomic write | Readers always see consistent state |
   900	| Lock: acquire → second acquire fails → release → second succeeds | Single-writer |
   901	| Lock: acquire → SIGKILL holder → new process detects stale lock (bootId or dead PID) → breaks → acquires | Stale lock detection |
   902	| Lock: acquire → SIGKILL holder → macOS reuses PID → bootId mismatch prevents false alive | PID reuse safety |
   903	| Lock: holder A releases → B acquires → A tries to release (stale handle) → inode mismatch prevents unlink | Cross-process unlink safety |
   904	| Corrupted lock file → `registry-locked` after timeout, NOT silent removal | Indeterminate state |
   905	| Write `maxRegistryEntries`, verify all readable, measure latency | Scale benchmark |
   906	
   907	### 7.2 Idempotency and ensure-launch
   908	
   909	| Test | Proves |
   910	| ---- | ------ |
   911	| `launchStaticGroup` same key+digest 10× → 1 execution, rest `"already-accepted"` | Idempotent launch |
   912	| Write `dispatch-intent`, SIGKILL before spawn → retry `launchStaticGroup` → progresses to `"launcher-started"`, spawns child | Ensure-launch recovery |
   913	| Same key, different digest → `"conflict"` | Conflict detection |
   914	| `stopLaunch` 5× → first `"stopping"`/`"stopped"`, rest `"already-terminal"` | Idempotent stop |
   915	| `acknowledgeRetention` 2× same digests → first deletes, second succeeds | Idempotent retention |
   916	
   917	### 7.3 Crash recovery (SIGKILL at each window)
   918	
   919	| Test | Proves |
   920	| ---- | ------ |
   921	| Kill after registry write, before reply → retry → `"already-accepted"` | Durable ack |
   922	| Kill after reply, before launcher spawn → retry → spawns launcher | Ensure-launch progress |
   923	| Kill after launcher spawn, before handshake → `inspectLaunch` detects dead PID → stale-run → `"failed"` | Launcher death detection |
   924	| Kill parent, launcher keeps running → new process `inspectLaunch` → `"running"` | Cross-process continuity |
   925	| Launcher writes result, kill parent → new process `readJobResult` → `"available"` with correct commitment | Non-destructive result |
   926	| `acknowledgeRetention` deletes 2/5 files, SIGKILL → retry → succeeds, 3 remaining deleted | Cleanup idempotency |
   927	
   928	### 7.4 Result integrity
   929	
   930	| Test | Proves |
   931	| ---- | ------ |
   932	| Write result → `readJobResult` → `resultCommitment` matches file | Basic integrity |
   933	| Write result → externally modify file → `readJobResult` → `IntegrityConflictError`, NOT silent update | Immutability enforcement |
   934	| Runner produces output at `rawOutputBytesPerJob` exactly → accepted | Limit upper bound |
   935	| Runner produces output at `rawOutputBytesPerJob + 1` → stopped at limit, job `"failed"`, structured error | Limit enforcement |
   936	| Binary content → job `"failed"` | UTF-8 enforcement |
   937	| `ArtifactTargetRefV1` with `..` in relativePath → rejected | Path confinement |
   938	| Symlink at result path pointing outside namespace → rejected | Symlink confinement |
   939	
   940	### 7.5 Full lifecycle integration test
   941	
   942	```
   943	capabilities() → all 7 booleans true
   944	
   945	launchStaticGroup(K, D, jobs) → { kind: "accepted", dependencyExecutionId, durableRecordCommitment }
   946	launchStaticGroup(K, D, jobs) → { kind: "already-accepted" }
   947	launchStaticGroup(K, D', jobs) → { kind: "conflict" }
   948	
   949	inspectLaunch(K) → { state: "running", snapshotCommitment }
   950	
   951	// Wait for completion...
   952	
   953	readJobResult(K, jobId) × each job → { kind: "available", resultCommitment }
   954	inspectLaunch(K) → { state: "completed" }
   955	
   956	acknowledgeRetention(K, digests) → { acknowledgedDigests, receiptCommitment }
   957	acknowledgeRetention(K, digests) → success (idempotent)
   958	```
   959	
   960	### 7.6 Ensure-launch (orphaned intent) integration test
   961	
   962	```
   963	launchStaticGroup(K, D, jobs) → { kind: "accepted" }
   964	
   965	// Simulate: registry written, but launcher spawn crashes
   966	// (manually revert state to "dispatch-intent" in registry)
   967	
   968	launchStaticGroup(K, D, jobs) → { kind: "already-accepted" }
   969	inspectLaunch(K) → { state: "launcher-started" } or "running"
   970	// A real child process was spawned this time.
   971	```
   972	
   973	---
   974	
   975	## 8. Resource Policy Integration
   976	
   977	Every tunable in the implementation MUST be resolved from
   978	`TurnlockResourcePolicy` (section 2.2). No hardcoded constants for limits,
   979	timeouts, grace periods, or capacities.
   980	
   981	The Turnlock adapter is responsible for constructing the policy from the
   982	committed `STD-TURNLOCK-DELEGATION-RESOURCE-POLICY` before calling
   983	`createTurnlockIntegration`.
   984	
   985	If the policy changes between runs (detected via `resourcePolicyDigest`),
   986	Turnlock creates a new `TurnlockIntegration` instance with the updated policy.
   987	The registry is policy-versioned via its `version` field.
   988	
   989	---
   990	
   991	## 9. Migration from Current API
   992	
   993	### 9.1 Backward compatibility
   994	
   995	The existing RPC event-bus interface (`registerSubagentRpcBridge`) and all
   996	interactive Pi functionality MUST continue to work unchanged. The Turnlock
   997	integration is a separate sub-path export.
   998	
   999	### 9.2 Sub-path contract
  1000	
  1001	```typescript
  1002	// Public, stable, side-effect-free on load.
  1003	import { createTurnlockIntegration } from "pi-subagents/turnlock";
  1004	```
  1005	
  1006	The sub-path MUST NOT:
  1007	
  1008	- Import or initialize the Pi extension (`ExtensionAPI`)
  1009	- Start the result watcher
  1010	- Register TUI components
  1011	- Touch `globalThis` singletons (background-work registry, etc.)
  1012	- Open files, create directories, or acquire locks at import time
  1013	
  1014	### 9.3 Result watcher coexistence
  1015	
  1016	Turnlock result files live under `<registryRoot>/launches/<id>/results/`,
  1017	completely outside `RESULTS_DIR`. No watcher modification needed.
  1018	
  1019	### 9.4 File structure
  1020	
  1021	```
  1022	<registryRoot>/                  ← Turnlock-allocated
  1023	├── lock
  1024	├── registry.json
  1025	└── launches/
  1026	    └── <dependencyExecutionId>/
  1027	        ├── async/               ← launcher working dir
  1028	        └── results/             ← job result files (write-once, retained until ack)
  1029	```
  1030	
  1031	---
  1032	
  1033	## 10. Non-Requirements (Explicit Exclusions)
  1034	
  1035	This specification does NOT require:
  1036	
  1037	- **Remote execution.** All launches run as local child processes.
  1038	- **Network resilience.** Assumes a local APFS filesystem.
  1039	- **Multi-machine coordination.** O_EXCL lock is local.
  1040	- **Exactly-once LLM execution.** Durability covers launch tracking and result
  1041	  retention, not LLM request deduplication.
  1042	- **Authentication / authorization.** Caller is a trusted local process.
  1043	- **Encryption at rest.**
  1044	- **Compression or archival.**
  1045	- **Graceful degradation under disk full.** Operations fail with filesystem
  1046	  errors. Atomic writes leave the registry consistent.
  1047	- **Registry backup or replication.**
  1048	- **Horizontal scaling.** One Turnlock instance, one registry.
  1049	
  1050	---
  1051	
  1052	## 11. Acceptance Checklist
  1053	
  1054	Before Turnlock's Dependency Contract can declare this implementation
  1055	compatible, ALL of the following MUST be true:
  1056	
  1057	- [ ] `capabilities()` returns all 7 capability booleans as `true`
  1058	- [ ] `sourceCommit` embedded at build time, matches inspected commit
  1059	- [ ] `registryRoot` is mandatory; no default, no env fallback
  1060	- [ ] Sub-path `pi-subagents/turnlock` has zero side effects on load
  1061	- [ ] `launchStaticGroup` is idempotent for equal key+digest
  1062	- [ ] `launchStaticGroup` returns `"conflict"` for divergent digest
  1063	- [ ] `launchStaticGroup` progresses orphaned `dispatch-intent` (ensure-launch)
  1064	- [ ] Registry entry is durable before `"accepted"` reply
  1065	- [ ] `inspectLaunch` returns correct state after process restart
  1066	- [ ] Stale-run reconciliation updates the durable registry
  1067	- [ ] Result files survive process crash and restart
  1068	- [ ] `readJobResult` never deletes or modifies result files
  1069	- [ ] Result immutability: modification → `IntegrityConflictError`, not silent update
  1070	- [ ] `ArtifactTargetRefV1` path confinement enforced (no `..`, no symlink escape)
  1071	- [ ] `stopLaunch` is idempotent and works after restart
  1072	- [ ] `acknowledgeRetention` deletes results only when explicitly called
  1073	- [ ] `acknowledgeRetention` is idempotent on retry
  1074	- [ ] All limits/timeouts/capacities resolved from `TurnlockResourcePolicy`, not hardcoded
  1075	- [ ] Lock: bootId + PID + nonce; stale detection uses both; inode check on release
  1076	- [ ] Corrupted lock file → `registry-locked`, not silent removal
  1077	- [ ] All test categories from section 7 pass against actual implementation
  1078	- [ ] Scale benchmark at policy max entries published
  1079	- [ ] Existing Pi subagent functionality unchanged
  1080	- [ ] No runtime dependency added beyond those already present in the fork
  1081	
  1082	---
  1083	
  1084	## A. Design Decisions
  1085	
  1086	### A.1 Why same-process, not Unix socket?
  1087	
  1088	The Turnlock Runner and Pi strategy adapter run in the same Bun process. A
  1089	direct TypeScript API is simpler, avoids serialization, and keeps the
  1090	dependency graph explicit. The socket becomes relevant only if/when Turnlock
  1091	and Pi run in separate processes.
  1092	
  1093	### A.2 Why ensure-launch semantics in launchStaticGroup?
  1094	
  1095	A separate `reconcileLaunch` operation was considered. Having
  1096	`launchStaticGroup` automatically progress an orphaned `dispatch-intent` is
  1097	simpler for the caller: the same idempotent call that creates a launch also
  1098	recovers a crashed one. The caller does not need to branch on `inspectLaunch`
  1099	output before retrying.
  1100	
  1101	### A.3 Why ArtifactTargetRefV1 instead of raw paths?
  1102	
  1103	Raw absolute paths allow the caller to write anywhere. `ArtifactTargetRefV1`
  1104	confines writes to a trusted root, enforces write-once semantics, and enables
  1105	integrity verification via `ArtifactCommitmentV2`. This matches Turnlock's
  1106	artifact system.
  1107	
  1108	### A.4 Why write-once + integrity conflict, not mutable results?
  1109	
  1110	Turnlock's `snapshot-authoritative` principle: facts, once established, cannot
  1111	be silently revised. If a result file changes after the initial write, this is
  1112	evidence of an integrity violation (disk corruption, external tampering, or
  1113	implementation bug), not a normal state update. Quarantine preserves the
  1114	evidence for operator disposition.
  1115	
  1116	### A.5 Why bootId in the lock file?
  1117	
  1118	macOS reuses PIDs. A stale lock check based on PID alone can falsely conclude
  1119	a dead holder is alive if the PID was recycled. `bootId + PID` eliminates this:
  1120	a recycled PID after a reboot has a different bootId. Within the same boot,
  1121	PID reuse is possible but extremely unlikely within the lock timeout; the
  1122	nonce provides an additional layer of defense.
  1123	
  1124	### A.6 Why fsync on temp file AND parent directory?
  1125	
  1126	`rename` is atomic on APFS, but without `fsync` on the parent directory, the
  1127	directory entry may not be persisted before a crash. The combination
  1128	`fsync(temp) → rename → fsync(parentDir)` guarantees that after a crash, either
  1129	the old file or the new file is visible, and the new file's contents are
  1130	complete.
  1131	
  1132	---
  1133	
  1134	## B. Field Mapping: API ↔ CDD-S
  1135	
  1136	| This spec field | CDD-S field | Notes |
  1137	| --------------- | ----------- | ----- |
  1138	| `LaunchReply.durableRecordCommitment` | `LaunchReplySketch.durableRecordCommitment` | Exact match |
  1139	| `LaunchSnapshot.snapshotCommitment` | `LaunchSnapshotSketch.snapshotCommitment` | Exact match |
  1140	| `JobResult.resultCommitment` | `JobResultSketch.resultCommitment` | Exact match |
  1141	| `StopReply.snapshotCommitment` | `StopReplySketch.snapshotCommitment` | Exact match |
  1142	| `RetentionReply.receiptCommitment` | `RetentionReplySketch.receiptCommitment` | Exact match |
  1143	| `LaunchJobRequest.rawResultTarget` | `LaunchJobRequestSketch.rawResultTarget` | Both `ArtifactTargetRefV1` |
  1144	| `LaunchRequest.callerLaunchKey` | `LaunchRequestSketch.callerLaunchKey` | Exact match |
  1145	| `LaunchRequest.requestDigest` | `LaunchRequestSketch.requestDigest` | Exact match |
  1146	| `DurableLaunchState` | `LaunchSnapshotSketch.state` | v2 adds `dispatch-intent`, `launcher-started`; removes `accepted` |
  1147	| `RegistryJobEntry.resultCommitment` | — | Internal; published via `JobResult.resultCommitment` |

    89	### 1.2 Registry entries
    90	
    91	One entry per launch, keyed by `callerLaunchKey`:
    92	
    93	```typescript
    94	interface RegistryFile {
    95	  readonly version: 2;
    96	  readonly entries: Record<string, RegistryEntry>;
    97	}
    98	
    99	interface RegistryEntry {
   100	  readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   101	  readonly requestDigest: string;             // hex SHA-256
   102	  readonly groupSpecDigest: string;           // hex SHA-256
   103	  readonly dependencyExecutionId: string;     // ULID
   104	  readonly state: DurableLaunchState;
   105	  readonly asyncDir: string;                  // absolute, under registryRoot
   106	  readonly resultNamespace: string;           // absolute root for job results
   107	  readonly jobs: Record<string, RegistryJobEntry>;
   108	  readonly launchPlan: LaunchPlan;            // immutable, complete
   109	  readonly createdAtEpochMs: number;
   110	  readonly updatedAtEpochMs: number;
   111	  // Present only when state is terminal:
   112	  readonly terminalAtEpochMs?: number;
   113	  // Present only if stopLaunch was called:
   114	  readonly stopRequestedAtEpochMs?: number;
   115	  readonly stopReason?: string;
   116	}
   117	
   118	/**
   119	 * Durable launch FSM.
   120	 *
   121	 *   dispatch-intent   ← registry written, no child process yet
   122	 *        │
   123	 *   launcher-started  ← child process spawned, PID recorded
   124	 *        │
   125	 *   running           ← handshake complete, agents executing
   126	 *        │
   127	 *   completed | failed | stopped   ← terminal
   128	 */
   129	type DurableLaunchState =
   130	  | "dispatch-intent"
   131	  | "launcher-started"
   132	  | "running"
   133	  | "completed"
   134	  | "failed"
   135	  | "stopped";
   136	
   137	/**
   138	 * Immutable launch plan. Stored in the registry at dispatch-intent time so
   139	 * that a recovery process can mechanically determine whether the launch was
   140	 * started, and if not, safely trigger it.
   141	 */
   142	interface LaunchPlan {
   143	  readonly version: 1;
   144	  readonly concurrency: number;
   145	  readonly deadlineAtEpochMs: number;
   146	  readonly jobs: readonly LaunchPlanJob[];
   147	}
   148	
   149	interface LaunchPlanJob {
   150	  readonly jobId: string;
   151	  readonly agentName: string;
   152	  readonly task: string;
   153	  readonly modelSelector: string;
   154	  readonly requestedThinking?: string;
   155	  readonly targetRef: ArtifactTargetRefV1;
   156	  readonly resultContractDigest?: string;
   157	}
   158	
   159	interface RegistryJobEntry {
   160	  readonly jobId: string;
   161	  readonly state: JobState;
   162	  readonly targetRef: ArtifactTargetRefV1;
   163	  /** Commitment published when the job reaches a terminal state. */
   164	  readonly resultCommitment?: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   165	  readonly terminalAtEpochMs?: number;
   166	}
   167	
   168	type JobState =
   169	  | "queued"
   170	  | "running"
   171	  | "completed"
   172	  | "failed"
   173	  | "stopped";
   174	```
   175	
   176	### 1.3 Atomic writes
   177	
   178	Every write to `registry.json` MUST use the pattern:
   179	
   180	```
   181	write temp file → fsync temp file → rename over target → fsync parent directory
   182	```
   183	
   184	The existing `writeAtomicJson` helper in `src/shared/atomic-json.ts` MUST be
   185	augmented with `fsync` on the file before rename and `fsync` on the parent
   186	directory after rename. On APFS, `rename` is atomic by design; the directory
   187	`fsync` guarantees the directory entry is persisted.
   188	
   189	### 1.4 Concurrency
   190	
   191	Single-writer via O_EXCL lock at `<registryRoot>/lock`. Readers do not need
   192	the lock (atomic rename guarantees consistent reads).
   193	
   194	The lock file MUST contain: `bootId`, `pid`, and a random `nonce`. Stale lock
   195	detection checks: `bootId` match AND `pid` alive. PID alone is insufficient
   196	(macOS reuses PIDs).
   197	
   198	The lock holder MUST NOT release a lock it did not acquire. Before `unlink`,
   199	verify the lock file's inode matches the one opened at acquisition. A corrupted
   200	or unreadable lock file MUST be treated as an indeterminate state, not silently
   201	removed.
   202	
   203	Lock timeout, lock acquisition retry interval, and stale lock grace period
   204	MUST be derived from the resource policy (section 8), not hardcoded.
   205	
   206	### 1.5 Registry scale
   207	
   208	The maximum number of concurrent entries and the maximum registry file size
   209	MUST be derived from the resource policy. The implementation MUST benchmark
   210	read/write performance at the policy-defined maximum and publish the results
   211	as part of the Dependency Contract evidence.
   212	
   213	Rewriting the entire registry file on every update is acceptable for the
   214	policy-defined scale. If the policy maximum exceeds what a single JSON file
   215	can handle, the storage design MUST be revisited (e.g., per-launch entry
   216	files with a manifest index).
   361	### 2.5 launchStaticGroup(request)
   362	
   363	```typescript
   364	interface LaunchJobRequest {
   365	  readonly jobId: string;
   366	  readonly agentName: string;
   367	  readonly task: string;
   368	  readonly modelSelector: string;
   369	  readonly requestedThinking?: string;
   370	  /** Turnlock-allocated, write-once, relative to a trusted root. */
   371	  readonly rawResultTarget: ArtifactTargetRefV1;
   372	  readonly resultContractDigest?: string;
   373	}
   374	
   375	interface LaunchRequest {
   376	  readonly apiVersion: "turnlock-pi-subagents-v1";
   377	  readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   378	  readonly requestDigest: string;
   379	  readonly groupSpecDigest: string;
   380	  readonly context: "fresh";
   381	  readonly failFast: false;
   382	  readonly concurrency: number;
   383	  readonly deadlineAtEpochMs: number;
   384	  readonly jobs: readonly LaunchJobRequest[];
   385	}
   386	
   387	type LaunchReply =
   388	  | {
   389	      readonly kind: "accepted";
   390	      readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   391	      readonly requestDigest: string;
   392	      readonly dependencyExecutionId: string;
   393	      /** Commitment to the durable registry record. */
   394	      readonly durableRecordCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   395	    }
   396	  | {
   397	      readonly kind: "already-accepted";
   398	      readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   399	      readonly requestDigest: string;
   400	      readonly dependencyExecutionId: string;
   401	      readonly durableRecordCommitment: ArtifactCommitmentV2;
   402	    }
   403	  | {
   404	      readonly kind: "conflict";
   405	      readonly callerLaunchKey: string;
   406	      readonly existingRequestDigest: string;
   407	    };
   408	```
   409	
   410	**Pre-conditions (validated synchronously, before any I/O):**
   411	
   412	- `callerLaunchKey` matches `/^[\w\-.\/:]{1,256}$/`, contains no `\0`
   413	- `requestDigest` and `groupSpecDigest` are exactly 64 lowercase hex chars
   414	- `jobs.length` ∈ [1, `resourcePolicy.maxJobsPerLaunch`]
   415	- All `jobId` values are unique within the request
   416	- All `rawResultTarget` resolve to distinct, confined paths under the launch
   417	  namespace root (see section 4)
   418	- `concurrency` ∈ [1, 4]
   419	- `deadlineAtEpochMs` > `Date.now()`
   420	
   421	**Algorithm:**
   422	
   423	1. Validate pre-conditions. Reject with `"invalid-request"` on failure.
   424	2. Acquire registry lock.
   425	3. Read `registry.json`.
   426	4. If an entry exists for `callerLaunchKey`:
   427	   a. If `entry.requestDigest === request.requestDigest`:
   428	      - If `entry.state === "dispatch-intent"`: this is a crashed-before-spawn
   429	        scenario. Progress: spawn launcher, transition to `"launcher-started"`,
   430	        write registry, release lock, return `"already-accepted"`.
   431	      - Otherwise: release lock, return `"already-accepted"`.
   432	   b. If `entry.requestDigest !== request.requestDigest`:
   433	      - Release lock, return `"conflict"`.
   434	5. Generate `dependencyExecutionId` (ULID).
   435	6. Build the immutable `LaunchPlan` from the request.
   436	7. Create `asyncDir` and `resultNamespace` under
   437	   `<registryRoot>/launches/<dependencyExecutionId>/`.
   438	8. Write registry entry with `state: "dispatch-intent"`, `launchPlan`, all jobs
   439	   in `"queued"` state:
   440	   - Atomic write (tmp + rename + fsync dir).
   441	9. Compute `durableRecordCommitment` = `ArtifactCommitmentV2` over the
   442	   written entry (digest of canonical JSON of the entry at rest).
   443	10. Spawn the launcher child process:
   444	    - Transition to `"launcher-started"`, record PID, write registry.
   445	11. Release lock.
   446	12. Return `{ kind: "accepted", ..., durableRecordCommitment }`.
   447	
   448	**Ensure-launch semantics:** `launchStaticGroup` is not just "create if
   449	absent." When called with a key in `"dispatch-intent"` state (written before
   450	a crash that killed the launcher), it MUST progress to `"launcher-started"`
   451	and spawn the child process. The launch plan is already in the registry; the
   452	implementation replays it deterministically.

   454	**Idempotency:** Same key+digest any number of times → exactly one execution
   455	group. Same key, different digest → `"conflict"` every time, no execution.

   489	      - Check each job's result target for a result file.
   490	      - Update job states and overall launch state based on evidence.
   491	      - Write updated registry (with lock).

   519	      - Compute `ArtifactCommitmentV2` (canonical JSON digest + byte size).

   521	        content), `resultCommitment`, `terminalAtEpochMs`.

   553

   559	   directly to `"stopped"`, mark all queued jobs as `"stopped"`. Write

   562	   a. Record `stopRequestedAtEpochMs`, `stopReason`. Write registry (so the
   563	      stop intent is durable even if we crash next).

   570	   h. For each non-terminal job, set state `"stopped"`, `terminalAtEpochMs`.

   703	## 4. Result Files
   704	
   705	### 4.1 ArtifactTargetRefV1 (not raw path strings)
   706	
   707	Turnlock allocates result targets using its artifact reference system:
   708	
   709	```typescript
   710	interface ArtifactTargetRefV1 {
   711	  readonly version: 1;
   712	  readonly root: "turnlock-run";
   713	  readonly allocationId: string;
   714	  readonly purpose: "strategy-raw-result";
   715	  readonly relativePath: string;
   716	}
   717	```
   718	
   719	The implementation MUST:
   720	
   721	1. Resolve `root` against the registry root (Turnlock provides the mapping).
   722	2. Validate that `relativePath` does not escape the root (no `..`, no
   723	   symlinks, no absolute components).
   724	3. Ensure the `allocationId` matches the launch namespace.
   725	4. Write exactly once — the file MUST NOT exist before writing.
   726	5. Publish an `ArtifactCommitmentV2` (canonical JSON digest + byte size) after
   727	   the write.
   728	
   729	### 4.2 Location
   730	
   731	Result files are written under
   732	`<registryRoot>/launches/<dependencyExecutionId>/results/`, resolved from the
   733	`ArtifactTargetRefV1`. This is OUTSIDE the standard `RESULTS_DIR` that the
   734	existing `result-watcher.ts` monitors. No watcher modification is needed.
   735	
   736	### 4.3 Format
   737	
   738	Valid UTF-8 JSON. Maximum `resourcePolicy.rawOutputBytesPerJob` bytes.
   739	
   740	If the runner output exceeds this limit: stop reading at the limit, mark the
   741	job `"failed"` with a structured error. Do NOT write truncated JSON (truncated
   742	JSON is often invalid and misleading). The error message MUST include the limit
   743	that was exceeded.
   744	
   745	Binary (non-UTF-8) content: mark job `"failed"`. Do not write an invalid
   746	result file.
   747	
   748	### 4.4 Immutability
   749	
   750	A result file is **write-once**. After the initial write, pi-subagents MUST NOT
   751	modify it. If `readJobResult` detects a change (digest mismatch from the
   752	recorded `resultCommitment`):
   753	
   754	- **Do NOT** update the registry's `resultCommitment`.
   755	- **Do NOT** treat it as a normal update.
   756	- Throw `IntegrityConflictError` with both the recorded and observed
   757	  commitments.
   758	- Turnlock treats this as a quarantine trigger.

   762	## 5. Concurrency and Locking
   763	
   764	### 5.1 Lock file format
   765	
   766	```typescript
   767	interface LockFile {
   768	  readonly bootId: string;
   769	  readonly pid: number;
   770	  readonly nonce: string;       // random, 16 hex chars
   771	  readonly acquiredAtEpochMs: number;
   772	}
   773	```
   774	
   775	### 5.2 Lock acquisition
   776	
   777	```typescript
   778	function acquireLock(
   779	  registryRoot: string,
   780	  policy: TurnlockResourcePolicy
   781	): LockHandle {
   782	  const lockPath = path.join(registryRoot, "lock");
   783	  const deadline = Date.now() + policy.lockTimeoutMs;
   784	
   785	  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
   786	    try {
   787	      const fd = fs.openSync(lockPath, "wx");  // O_EXCL
   788	      const lockFile: LockFile = {
   789	        bootId: getBootId(),
   790	        pid: process.pid,
   791	        nonce: randomHex(16),
   792	        acquiredAtEpochMs: Date.now(),
   793	      };
   794	      fs.writeSync(fd, JSON.stringify(lockFile));
   795	      fs.fsyncSync(fd);
   796	      return {
   797	        fd,
   798	        path: lockPath,
   799	        inode: fs.fstatSync(fd).ino,
   800	        nonce: lockFile.nonce,
   801	      };
   802	    } catch (err) {
   803	      if (err.code !== "EEXIST") throw err;
   804	      const existing = readLockFile(lockPath);
   805	      if (existing === null) {
   806	        // Corrupted lock file — indeterminate state. Do NOT remove blindly.
   807	        sleepSync(policy.lockRetryIntervalMs);
   808	        continue;
   809	      }
   810	      if (!isLockHolderValid(existing, policy.staleLockGraceMs)) {
   811	        // Stale lock: bootId mismatch or PID dead past grace period.
   812	        try { fs.unlinkSync(lockPath); } catch {}
   813	        continue;
   814	      }
   815	      // Valid lock held by another process. Wait.
   816	      sleepSync(policy.lockRetryIntervalMs);
   817	    }
   818	  }
   819	  throw new TurnlockIntegrationError("registry-locked",
   820	    `Could not acquire registry lock within ${policy.lockTimeoutMs}ms.`);
   821	}
   822	```
   823	
   824	### 5.3 Lock release
   825	
   826	```typescript
   827	function releaseLock(handle: LockHandle): void {
   828	  // Verify we still own this lock file (inode match).
   829	  let currentIno: number | undefined;
   830	  try { currentIno = fs.statSync(handle.path).ino; } catch { return; }
   831	  if (currentIno !== handle.inode) return; // Replaced by another process.
   832	
   833	  try { fs.closeSync(handle.fd); } catch {}
   834	  try { fs.unlinkSync(handle.path); } catch {}
   835	}
   836	```
   837	
   838	### 5.4 Lock lifecycle
   839	
   840	- `process.on("exit", () => releaseLock(activeLock))` for normal exit.
   841	- Every lock acquisition is wrapped in try/finally with release in the finally
   842	  block.
   843	- If the process crashes, stale lock detection (bootId + PID liveness) allows
   844	  the next process to break it.

   892	## 7. Test Requirements
   893	
   894	### 7.1 Registry durability
   895	
   896	| Test | Proves |
   897	| ---- | ------ |

   899	| 10 concurrent `inspectLaunch` during atomic write | Readers always see consistent state |
   900	| Lock: acquire → second acquire fails → release → second succeeds | Single-writer |
   901	| Lock: acquire → SIGKILL holder → new process detects stale lock (bootId or dead PID) → breaks → acquires | Stale lock detection |
   902	| Lock: acquire → SIGKILL holder → macOS reuses PID → bootId mismatch prevents false alive | PID reuse safety |
   903	| Lock: holder A releases → B acquires → A tries to release (stale handle) → inode mismatch prevents unlink | Cross-process unlink safety |
   904	| Corrupted lock file → `registry-locked` after timeout, NOT silent removal | Indeterminate state |
   905	| Write `maxRegistryEntries`, verify all readable, measure latency | Scale benchmark |
   906

   908	
   909	| Test | Proves |
   910	| ---- | ------ |

   912	| Write `dispatch-intent`, SIGKILL before spawn → retry `launchStaticGroup` → progresses to `"launcher-started"`, spawns child | Ensure-launch recovery |

   919	| Test | Proves |
   920	| ---- | ------ |
   921	| Kill after registry write, before reply → retry → `"already-accepted"` | Durable ack |
   922	| Kill after reply, before launcher spawn → retry → spawns launcher | Ensure-launch progress |
   923	| Kill after launcher spawn, before handshake → `inspectLaunch` detects dead PID → stale-run → `"failed"` | Launcher death detection |

   930	| Test | Proves |

   932	| Write result → `readJobResult` → `resultCommitment` matches file | Basic integrity |
   933	| Write result → externally modify file → `readJobResult` → `IntegrityConflictError`, NOT silent update | Immutability enforcement |

   937	| `ArtifactTargetRefV1` with `..` in relativePath → rejected | Path confinement |

   176	### 1.3 Atomic writes
   177	
   178	Every write to `registry.json` MUST use the pattern:
   179	
   180	```
   181	write temp file → fsync temp file → rename over target → fsync parent directory
   182	```
   183	
   184	The existing `writeAtomicJson` helper in `src/shared/atomic-json.ts` MUST be
   185	augmented with `fsync` on the file before rename and `fsync` on the parent
   186	directory after rename. On APFS, `rename` is atomic by design; the directory
   187	`fsync` guarantees the directory entry is persisted.
   188	
   189	### 1.4 Concurrency
   190	
   191	Single-writer via O_EXCL lock at `<registryRoot>/lock`. Readers do not need
   192	the lock (atomic rename guarantees consistent reads).
   193	
   194	The lock file MUST contain: `bootId`, `pid`, and a random `nonce`. Stale lock
   195	detection checks: `bootId` match AND `pid` alive. PID alone is insufficient
   196	(macOS reuses PIDs).
   197	
   198	The lock holder MUST NOT release a lock it did not acquire. Before `unlink`,
   199	verify the lock file's inode matches the one opened at acquisition. A corrupted
   200	or unreadable lock file MUST be treated as an indeterminate state, not silently
   201	removed.
   202	
   203	Lock timeout, lock acquisition retry interval, and stale lock grace period
   204	MUST be derived from the resource policy (section 8), not hardcoded.
   205	
   206	### 1.5 Registry scale
   207	
   208	The maximum number of concurrent entries and the maximum registry file size
   209	MUST be derived from the resource policy. The implementation MUST benchmark
   210	read/write performance at the policy-defined maximum and publish the results
   211	as part of the Dependency Contract evidence.
   212	
   213	Rewriting the entire registry file on every update is acceptable for the
   214	policy-defined scale. If the policy maximum exceeds what a single JSON file
   215	can handle, the storage design MUST be revisited (e.g., per-launch entry
   216	files with a manifest index).

   441	9. Compute `durableRecordCommitment` = `ArtifactCommitmentV2` over the
   442	   written entry (digest of canonical JSON of the entry at rest).
   443	10. Spawn the launcher child process:
   444	    - Transition to `"launcher-started"`, record PID, write registry.
   445	11. Release lock.

   449	absent." When called with a key in `"dispatch-intent"` state (written before

   452	implementation replays it deterministically.

   512	
   513	1. Read `registry.json`.
   514	2. If no entry for `callerLaunchKey`, throw `LaunchNotFoundError`.
   515	3. If no job with `jobId`, throw `JobNotFoundError`.
   516	4. If job state is `"queued"` or `"running"`:
   517	   a. Check if a result file exists at the resolved `targetRef` path.
   518	   b. If yes and valid (UTF-8 JSON, ≤ `resourcePolicy.rawOutputBytesPerJob`):

   521	        content), `resultCommitment`, `terminalAtEpochMs`.

   553

   557	4. If `entry.state` is terminal: release lock, return `"already-terminal"`.
   558	5. If `entry.state` is `"dispatch-intent"`: no process to kill. Transition
   559	   directly to `"stopped"`, mark all queued jobs as `"stopped"`. Write

   562	   a. Record `stopRequestedAtEpochMs`, `stopReason`. Write registry (so the
   563	      stop intent is durable even if we crash next).
   564	   b. Release lock.

   570	   h. For each non-terminal job, set state `"stopped"`, `terminalAtEpochMs`.
   571	   i. Write atomic registry.
   572	   j. Release lock.
   573	   k. Return `"stopped"` with `snapshotCommitment`.

   703	## 4. Result Files
   704	
   705	### 4.1 ArtifactTargetRefV1 (not raw path strings)
   706	
   707	Turnlock allocates result targets using its artifact reference system:
   708	
   709	```typescript
   710	interface ArtifactTargetRefV1 {
   711	  readonly version: 1;
   712	  readonly root: "turnlock-run";
   713	  readonly allocationId: string;
   714	  readonly purpose: "strategy-raw-result";
   715	  readonly relativePath: string;
   716	}
   717	```
   718	
   719	The implementation MUST:
   720	
   721	1. Resolve `root` against the registry root (Turnlock provides the mapping).
   722	2. Validate that `relativePath` does not escape the root (no `..`, no
   723	   symlinks, no absolute components).
   724	3. Ensure the `allocationId` matches the launch namespace.
   725	4. Write exactly once — the file MUST NOT exist before writing.
   726	5. Publish an `ArtifactCommitmentV2` (canonical JSON digest + byte size) after
   727	   the write.
   728	
   729	### 4.2 Location
   730	
   731	Result files are written under
   732	`<registryRoot>/launches/<dependencyExecutionId>/results/`, resolved from the
   733	`ArtifactTargetRefV1`. This is OUTSIDE the standard `RESULTS_DIR` that the
   734	existing `result-watcher.ts` monitors. No watcher modification is needed.
   735	
   736	### 4.3 Format
   737	
   738	Valid UTF-8 JSON. Maximum `resourcePolicy.rawOutputBytesPerJob` bytes.
   739	
   740	If the runner output exceeds this limit: stop reading at the limit, mark the
   741	job `"failed"` with a structured error. Do NOT write truncated JSON (truncated
   742	JSON is often invalid and misleading). The error message MUST include the limit
   743	that was exceeded.
   744	
   745	Binary (non-UTF-8) content: mark job `"failed"`. Do not write an invalid
   746	result file.
   747	
   748	### 4.4 Immutability
   749	
   750	A result file is **write-once**. After the initial write, pi-subagents MUST NOT
   751	modify it. If `readJobResult` detects a change (digest mismatch from the
   752	recorded `resultCommitment`):
   753	
   754	- **Do NOT** update the registry's `resultCommitment`.
   755	- **Do NOT** treat it as a normal update.
   756	- Throw `IntegrityConflictError` with both the recorded and observed
   757	  commitments.
   758	- Turnlock treats this as a quarantine trigger.

   762	## 5. Concurrency and Locking
   763	
   764	### 5.1 Lock file format
   765	
   766	```typescript
   767	interface LockFile {
   768	  readonly bootId: string;
   769	  readonly pid: number;
   770	  readonly nonce: string;       // random, 16 hex chars
   771	  readonly acquiredAtEpochMs: number;
   772	}
   773	```
   774	
   775	### 5.2 Lock acquisition
   776	
   777	```typescript
   778	function acquireLock(
   779	  registryRoot: string,
   780	  policy: TurnlockResourcePolicy
   781	): LockHandle {
   782	  const lockPath = path.join(registryRoot, "lock");
   783	  const deadline = Date.now() + policy.lockTimeoutMs;
   784	
   785	  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
   786	    try {
   787	      const fd = fs.openSync(lockPath, "wx");  // O_EXCL
   788	      const lockFile: LockFile = {
   789	        bootId: getBootId(),
   790	        pid: process.pid,
   791	        nonce: randomHex(16),
   792	        acquiredAtEpochMs: Date.now(),
   793	      };
   794	      fs.writeSync(fd, JSON.stringify(lockFile));
   795	      fs.fsyncSync(fd);
   796	      return {
   797	        fd,
   798	        path: lockPath,
   799	        inode: fs.fstatSync(fd).ino,
   800	        nonce: lockFile.nonce,
   801	      };
   802	    } catch (err) {
   803	      if (err.code !== "EEXIST") throw err;
   804	      const existing = readLockFile(lockPath);
   805	      if (existing === null) {
   806	        // Corrupted lock file — indeterminate state. Do NOT remove blindly.
   807	        sleepSync(policy.lockRetryIntervalMs);
   808	        continue;
   809	      }
   810	      if (!isLockHolderValid(existing, policy.staleLockGraceMs)) {
   811	        // Stale lock: bootId mismatch or PID dead past grace period.
   812	        try { fs.unlinkSync(lockPath); } catch {}
   813	        continue;
   814	      }
   815	      // Valid lock held by another process. Wait.
   816	      sleepSync(policy.lockRetryIntervalMs);
   817	    }
   818	  }
   819	  throw new TurnlockIntegrationError("registry-locked",
   820	    `Could not acquire registry lock within ${policy.lockTimeoutMs}ms.`);
   821	}
   822	```
   823	
   824	### 5.3 Lock release
   825	
   826	```typescript
   827	function releaseLock(handle: LockHandle): void {
   828	  // Verify we still own this lock file (inode match).
   829	  let currentIno: number | undefined;
   830	  try { currentIno = fs.statSync(handle.path).ino; } catch { return; }
   831	  if (currentIno !== handle.inode) return; // Replaced by another process.
   832	
   833	  try { fs.closeSync(handle.fd); } catch {}
   834	  try { fs.unlinkSync(handle.path); } catch {}
   835	}
   836	```

   838	### 5.4 Lock lifecycle
   839	
   840	- `process.on("exit", () => releaseLock(activeLock))` for normal exit.
   841	- Every lock acquisition is wrapped in try/finally with release in the finally
   842	  block.
   843	- If the process crashes, stale lock detection (bootId + PID liveness) allows
   844	  the next process to break it.

   892	## 7. Test Requirements
   893	
   894	### 7.1 Registry durability
   895	
   896	| Test | Proves |
   897	| ---- | ------ |

   899	| 10 concurrent `inspectLaunch` during atomic write | Readers always see consistent state |
   900	| Lock: acquire → second acquire fails → release → second succeeds | Single-writer |
   901	| Lock: acquire → SIGKILL holder → new process detects stale lock (bootId or dead PID) → breaks → acquires | Stale lock detection |
   902	| Lock: acquire → SIGKILL holder → macOS reuses PID → bootId mismatch prevents false alive | PID reuse safety |
   903	| Lock: holder A releases → B acquires → A tries to release (stale handle) → inode mismatch prevents unlink | Cross-process unlink safety |
   904	| Corrupted lock file → `registry-locked` after timeout, NOT silent removal | Indeterminate state |
   905	| Write `maxRegistryEntries`, verify all readable, measure latency | Scale benchmark |
